published_statement: (Restatement, L02 p6, eq. 3.75, G=c=1 restored) P = (G/5c^5) < dddQ_ij dddQ_ij >, Q_ij the traceless mass quadrupole, equivalently (G/5c^5)< dddM_ij dddM_ij - (1/3)(dddM_kk)^2 >, M^ij = int d^3x T^00 x^i x^j; <> an average over several GW periods, derivatives at retarded time. For a fixed circular rotator (L03 p2-3) omega_GW = 2 omega_s and P = (32/5) G mu^2 R^4 omega_s^6/c^5; the rod coefficient 2/45 is not printed in the source read -- it follows from mu R^2 -> M l^2/12 and is RE-DERIVED here.
published_hypotheses: linearised gravity about flat spacetime (box hbar_{mu nu} = -16 pi T_{mu nu}), weak field
non-relativistic (slow-motion) source, v << c, equivalently source size d << lambda_GW (L02 p2: omega x' n ~ v)
leading order of the multipole / post-Newtonian expansion only (corrections O(v/c): mass octupole, current quadrupole)
far zone r >> lambda, TT projection
stress-energy conserved, d_mu T^{mu nu} = 0, with T = 0 on the boundary of a volume enclosing the source (isolated source)
power is a time average over several GW periods
hypothesis_drift: NONE DROPPED from the formula: branelink.py:28-36/199-201 use the total, period-averaged luminosity of a slow, weak-field, isolated source in flat background; the tree's list (weak-field slow-motion, thin uniform rod, flat background) covers the source's hypotheses, with 'isolated source, d_mu T^{mu nu}=0 in flat space' implicit in 'flat background'. The rod's internal stresses enter T^ij and are what the flat-space conservation argument requires (L02 p3), so a non-gravitationally bound rod is inside the source's class.

ADDED, unnamed as a limitation (branelink.py:204-206, strain(); feeds STRAIN_H at branelink.py:216,299): isotropic emission, L/(4 pi D^2), and a circular-polarisation amplitude convention (<hd+^2+hdx^2> = w^2 h^2). The source's pattern (L03 p2) is anisotropic: face-on flux = 5/2 of the isotropic mean, edge-on = 5/16 (computed). So the tree's h is an orientation-averaged figure; the on-axis amplitude is sqrt(5/2) = 1.581 x larger (6.856e-48 vs 4.336e-48). Throughput per watt (bulk_bits_per_watt) is flux-based and moves by x5/16 .. x5/2 = -0.505 .. +0.398 dex with receiver orientation. The step is written in the docstring (branelink.py:205) but not carried as a named hypothesis.

ADDED, implicit (branelink.py:17-51): the 4D GR quadrupole formula is applied to O6's 'bulk channel'. The source is 4D GR; the tree itself makes this conditional in its dichotomy (branelink.py:43-51, 'graviton IS a bulk degree of freedom') and concedes 'no moving-brane emission rate is in print' -- named at the row level, not on this entry's hypothesis list.

WEAKENED, not named: 'thin' rod. For a solid cylinder of radius a the radiating moment is M(l^2/12 - a^2/4), multiplying L by (1 - 3a^2/l^2)^2 (sympy); the tree's M, l give no radius, so the thin limit is an unstated idealisation (correction < 1% only for a < 0.058 l).

UNNAMED physical hypothesis at the design point (branelink.py:135): a rod of l = 100 m at Omega = 100 rad/s must carry a centre stress sigma/rho = Omega^2 l^2/8 = 1.25e7 J/kg (computed). Whether any material sustains it is not checked here against material data (OPEN, not a finding). It does not enter the formula; if violated, a lower Omega RAISES bits/s/W as 1/Omega^2, and closing the 26.6-dex gap would need Omega lower by ~10^13 -- the direction is not moved.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. Einstein (1918) had no gravitational-wave data at all: no binary pulsar (1974), no double pulsar (2003), no interferometric detection (2015). Evidence AGAINST the missing data changing this conclusion: (a) the formula is a theorem of linearised GR re-derived here in closed form, with no empirical input except G; (b) every later measurement read agrees with the leading-order (quadrupole) flux -- Hulse-Taylor damping within 0.5% (Will 2014), and the double pulsar gives the tightest Newtonian-order bound (GWTC-5.0 p.15); (c) the one datum, G, moved 3.3e-5 relative since CODATA 2014 and is unchanged 2018->2022. Evidence the other way / what remains untested: all confirmations are for gravitationally bound astrophysical sources; no laboratory (stress-supported) source has ever been detected, so the rod case rests on the theorem, not on a measurement of a rod -- but it is the case the linearised derivation covers most directly (L02 p3 conservation argument), and at the design point v/c ~ 1.7e-5 so post-Newtonian corrections are ~1e-5. Historical note NOT used in the grade: the literature reports errors in Einstein's own 1916/1918 coefficients later corrected; not read here (NAMED-NOT-READ), and the tree uses the modern G/5c^5, which is what was re-derived.
grade_evidence: Statement and hypotheses READ via restatement (Gerosa lecture notes following Maggiore eq. 3.75; circular rotator L03 pp2-3); the tree's use (total, period-averaged luminosity; omega_GW = 2 Omega; coefficient 2/45) lies inside the source's class -- slow motion (v/c = 1.7e-5), long wavelength (lambda/l = 9.4e4), weak field, isolated stress-supported source in flat background. Independent sympy re-derivation agrees (2/45 in both forms, via the binary map, and omega_GW = 2 Omega by Fourier content); design-point numbers reproduce branelink. The only moved datum (G) moves the result by 3.3e-5. Recorded, NOT counted against the result: the downstream strain() uses an isotropic-average, circular-polarisation convention not named as a hypothesis (on-axis h larger by sqrt(5/2); bits/s/W span -0.505..+0.398 dex with orientation), a thin-rod idealisation (1-3a^2/l^2)^2, and an unchecked rod-integrity requirement (1.25e7 J/kg); none moves O6's 26.6-dex direction. Caveat on completeness: the original (Einstein 1918) and the textbook are NAMED-NOT-READ, and the later-literature search could not be run (alphaXiv quota).
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if the ledger treats STRAIN_H as an on-axis or orientation-independent amplitude (it is an isotropic-average; the orientation factor is sqrt(5/16)..sqrt(5/2) in h) or needs a thick rod (a not << l); OPEN-ing of the rod-integrity hypothesis if a material-strength check shows no material sustains Omega^2 l^2/8 = 1.25e7 J/kg (changes the design point, not the formula, and moves bits/W the favourable way only by 1/Omega^2); a READ of Einstein 1918 would settle attribution only; WRONG would need a computed contradiction of the linearised-GR derivation for slow isolated sources, of which none was found or produced.
